title: Creamy Garlic Chicken
description: Golden, crisp-skinned chicken thighs in a garlic, thyme and Parmesan cream sauce. One pan, thirty-five minutes.
intro: This is the weeknight dinner that never feels like a compromise. Chicken thighs stay juicy, the skin goes crisp in the pan, and the sauce is built in the same pan from all the flavour left behind.
Serve it with crusty bread, rice or buttered greens. There will be sauce left over, and someone will fight you for it.

items.item: dry white wine or chicken stock

method.title: Crisp the skin
method.text: Pat the chicken dry and season well. Place skin-side down in a large, cold frying pan with the oil, then set over a medium heat. Cook without moving for 12–14 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.

method.title: Cook through
method.text: Turn the thighs and cook for 5 more minutes until cooked through (74°C in the thickest part). Lift onto a plate, skin-side up.

method.title: Garlic
method.text: Pour off all but 1 tbsp of fat. Lower the heat, add the garlic and cook gently for 1–2 minutes until soft and just golden. Don't let it burn.

method.title: Build the sauce
method.text: Add the wine or stock and scrape up the browned bits. Bubble for 2 minutes, then stir in the cream, Parmesan, mustard and thyme. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until thickened.

method.title: Finish
method.text: Stir through the spinach until wilted, add a squeeze of lemon and season. Return the chicken, skin-side up, so the skin stays crisp above the sauce. Serve straight away.

tips: Starting the thighs in a cold pan renders the fat slowly and gives you the crispest skin.
Keep the skin above the sauce when you return the chicken, or it will soften.

substitutions.note: Crème fraîche works; stir it in off the heat so it doesn't split.
Use breasts, flattened slightly, and cook for 5–6 minutes per side.
Any hard, aged cheese such as Grana Padano or mature Cheddar.
